Predeclared and launched the next diagnostic on the same observed OASIS 11 fine-start checkpoint: source-trilinear intensity derivatives multiplied by the exact affine Jacobian, symmetric residual-map vertex Jacobian, and work-grid physical covector transform. The production optimizer and gradient remain unchanged. This tests the spatial/composition discretization hypothesis using the same three directions, eight epsilons, 0.005 symmetric relative error and three-point decreasing-error criterion. All nonzero intensity derivatives must have usable spatial support; missing derivatives and source-grid knots are counted explicitly. Simultaneous source/residual kinks are not claimed to have a unique linear derivative. The earlier 24 finite-difference and intensity-chain measurements are pinned for exact reproduction.

Provider-first review found scalar linear sampling in image4s ReferenceSampler and Sobel/Scharr discrete image stencils in image4s Gradient, but no arbitrary-coordinate interpolant derivative in those inspected APIs. The local diagnostic differentiates the existing HalfFlow sampling polynomial without adding a new geometry owner. Four new tests cover exact trilinear polynomials, counted symmetric knot slopes, unavailable/zero-weight support, and actual paired composition on mixed oblique grids for symmetric and fixed-anchor actions. All seven focused tests (four spatial plus three frozen-objective) pass on JVM and Scala.js; runner compilation passes. A first compiler error from using four indices on a scalar rank-three image was corrected and its log retained. Frozen numerical source a3827bfdff07a34f5c54f5229ab92b515b1b20bf45fbf80751baa228c3f7afaf is running in spatial-chain-pilot-v1. No acquired-image result or anatomical improvement is yet claimed.

The first 29-state export batch continues. Its analysis follower resumes only when new export receipts arrive and never restarts registration or export processes. All fitting/export/scoring walltimes remain diagnostic and excluded from production performance comparisons.
